name: Brian T Nava

bio.statement: The county treasurer page says Nava was elected Clackamas County Treasurer in November 2018.
bio.excerpt: Brian Nava was elected as Clackamas County's Treasurer in November of 2018.

bio.statement: The treasurer page says Nava was appointed the county's first internal auditor in August 2015.
bio.excerpt: Prior to his election as County Treasurer, Brian was appointed as Clackamas County's first Internal Auditor in August 2015.

bio.statement: The treasurer page says Nava held audit positions with the Oregon Secretary of State Audits Division from 2004 to 2015.
bio.excerpt: Brian has also held various audit positions with the Oregon Secretary of State Audits Division from 2004 to 2015.

bio.statement: Nava's pamphlet statement lists a B.S. in accounting from Linfield College and an EMT certificate from Clackamas Community College.
bio.excerpt: Linfield College, B.S. Accounting, minors in Computer Science and Math. Clackamas CC, EMT Certificate

bio.statement: Nava's pamphlet statement says he has been a volunteer firefighter for over 15 years and served as the association's treasurer and president.
bio.excerpt: Brian has been a Volunteer Firefighter for over 15 years and served as the Association’s Treasurer and President.

positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Nava says he will continue prudent investing so county funds are safe, liquid and earn the best possible return.
positions.excerpt: Brian will continue Treasury's prudent investing, by ensuring funds are safe, liquid, and achieve the best return possible.

positions.statement: Nava's pamphlet statement says he has led the treasurer's office to introduce and improve banking functions.
positions.excerpt: Brian has led the Treasurer’s office to introduce and improve many banking functions.

positions.statement: Nava's pamphlet statement says he has helped find cost savings and recommended ways for the county to streamline its services.
positions.excerpt: Brian has helped find cost savings and made recommendations to help the County streamline and improve its services.
